newsitem.title: UK: Once-swinging Carnaby Street sold for $148 million.
newsitem.headline: Once-swinging Carnaby Street sold for $148 million.

text.p: London's Carnaby Street, a byword for fashion in the 1960s when the British capital was the world centre of popular culture, was sold for 90 million pounds ($148 million) on Thursday.
British property company Shaftesbury Plc said it had bought Carnaby Estate -- 93 properties in and around Carnaby Street in London's West End -- from the Dutch property fund Wereldhave.
The Dutch company announced earlier this year that it wanted to sell. It gave no reason.

Shaftesbury specialises in properties in the busy retail and tourist areas in central London. Its portfolio includes shops and restaurants in trendy Covent Garden and the Chinatown area near Leicester Square.

More than half of the 28 million tourists who visit London each year head still for Carnaby Street to catch an echo of the 1960s. These days it is little more than a tawdry extension of the capital's main shopping thoroughfare, Oxford Street, selling downmarket souvenirs and cheap T-shirts.
However, film, television and media companies have their offices in the area and annual rental income for Carnaby Street has been estimated at around 5.8 million pounds. ($1=.6093 Pound)
